article_sentences: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction.
The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

stories.title: Political storm hits Odisha in cyclone Arnab’s aftermath
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Even as Ganjam, Odisha’s most populous district, struggles to recover from the devastation of cyclone Arnab’s aftermath, a political storm is brewing over the government’s handling of the natural disaster.
Politically, the state is crucial as it helped power the BjP’s rise to power and is seen as its stronghold.

Allegations of a delayed response and inadequate relief measures have put the ruling BJP on the defensive, with videos surfacing of ministers and BJP MLAs facing public backlash during visits to affected areas.

Posters branding BJD president Naveen Patnaik as “missing” have also surfaced in his Hinjili constituency, one of the worst-affected areas, giving the BJP an opportunity to question the former Chief Minister’s response to the crisis in his own backyard.
The disaster has also triggered a war of words between the ruling party and the Opposition on social media.

While the BJD has termed the floods a “man-made disaster”, accusing the BJP government of mismanagement that pushed lakhs of people into distress, the BJP has sought to turn the spotlight on Patnaik’s absence from his constituency.
Criticising Patnaik for not visiting Hinjili, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Mukesh Mahaling.
“The BJD social media accounts are being used to troll, claiming that the government is failing to achieve anything and that its ministers are not monitoring affairs effectively.
I would ask them to introspect their own situation.
Why hasn’t the Leader of Opposition visited his own constituency?” Mahaling said.
Senior BJP leader Biranchi Narayan Tripathy on Wednesday slammed the previous BJD government’s lack of flood-control measures and poor management of river banks and dams.
Ganjam, along with neighbouring Gajapati and Kandhamal districts, has witnessed one of its worst floods in 36 years, reviving memories of the 1990 floods in the Rushikulya river basin.

stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rains wreak havoc in Aswaropet, Dammapeta and other mandals of Bhadradri Kothagudem
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Heavy rains triggered by Cyclone Murasu wreaked havoc in Aswaraopet, Dammapeta and several other mandals of Bhadradri Kothagudem district on Wednesday, inundating vast stretches of agricultural land and disrupting vehicular movement on several roads.

According to sources, the temporary ring bund of the Peddavagu medium irrigation project in Aswaraopet mandal reportedly suffered a breach, resulting in the inundation of agricultural fields in nearby villages.
Ponds and streams across the mandal swelled following overnight heavy downpour, causing waterlogging in low-lying areas of Aswaraopet, Naramvarigudem and other places.
Nemalipeta colony in Dammapeta was also inundated with rainwater, causing severe inconvenience to residents.
Vehicular movement on the Palvancha-Dammapeta road came to a standstill after a diversion road near Rajupeta in Mulakalapalli mandal was washed away by floodwaters on Wednesday morning.
Standing paddy and cotton crops, besides harvested produce were reportedly damaged by the heavy rains across several parts of the erstwhile undivided Khammam district, dealing a blow to farmers.
Local holidays were declared for schools in some mandals on Wednesday in view of the heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu.

stories.title: Cyclone Murasu impact on Telangana | Extremely heavy rains lash Bhadradri on November 4
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A mandal each in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem in Telangana, which were under red alert due to the impact of cyclone Murasu on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), received extremely heavy rainfall between 204 mm and 235 mm on the intervening night of Tuesday and Wednesday (November 3 and 4, 2026).
And, some more mandals in the two districts received very heavy rainfall between 150 mm and 204 mm.

Of the two, Bhadradri Kothagudem did not get a break from the extremely heavy rain on Wednesday as a mandal there received 278.5 mm, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s rainfall data till 8.00 p.m.
The highest of 278.5 mm in Aswaraopet was followed by 188.3 mm in Malkaram in Dammapeta mandal, 175 mm in Ankampalem in Dammapeta and 149.8 mm in Mulakalapally.
India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centres in its impact weather bulletin issued at 11 a.m. has placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under orange alert indicating heavy to very heavy rain on Wednesday.
Moderate to heavy rain was predicted in Mulugu and Khammam.
The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP.
I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial.

The highest of 235 mm in Mulakapalle of Bhadradri Kothagudem was followed by 204.7 mm in Vemsoor of Khammam, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report issued in the morning on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

article_sentences: A controversy has erupted in Odisha after a BJP MLA from Asika, Saroj Padhi, was accused by an IAS officer of misbehaving with and threatening him while he was deployed on flood management duty.
The officer submitted a police complaint against the legislator on Thursday.

Samir Kumar Jena, a 2022-batch IAS officer currently posted as chief development officer-cum-executive officer, zilla parishad, Ganjam, alleged in his complaint that Padhi entered his chamber on Tuesday and shouted at him over the distribution of relief materials.
Jena had been assigned to oversee relief and restoration work in the Asika area.

The IAS officer did not respond to calls seeking comment on the allegations, while a senior police officer in the district said the complaint was being verified and appropriate action would be taken in due course.
The MLA, on his part, said the matter had been “resolved”.
According to the complaint, Jena told the MLA that the relief materials had been arranged by Minister Bibhuti Jena and distributed to beneficiaries as instructed.
“The MLA continued to shout at me even when I tried to convince him to discuss the matter with the minister and to resolve the matter.
When I tried to explain my role here as an officer, he continued to hurl abuse at me using unparliamentary language and even threatened to kill me.
The MLA also shouted at me, asking me to leave the place,” the complainant alleged.
Jena further claimed that the alleged incident was captured on CCTV in the executive officer’s (EO) chamber.
“Because of this incident, I am highly demoralised and in deep mental shock,” he noted in the complaint.

stories.headline: How 3D Visual Models Can Make Flood Preparedness Training More Practical in Assam
stories.title: How 3D Visual Models Can Make Flood Preparedness Training More Practical in Assam
stories.summary: Flood preparedness is difficult to teach through instructions alone. A resident may understand a warning in principle but still struggle to picture how rising water could affect the road to a shelter, where medicines should be stored or why one household may need more time to evacuate than another. In Assam, where floods repeatedly disrupt homes, transport and education, preparedness activities need to turn general advice into decisions people can recognise. Simple 3D visual models can support that process by giving students and community members something concrete to examine, question and rearrange. An AI 3D generator can help educators create initial models of objects such as raised houses, relief boats, emergency supply boxes and temporary shelters from written descriptions. Meshy works through a browser and can export generated assets for further editing. The free plan is enough to generate and preview models; downloading them requires a paid plan. These models can support lesson planning and tabletop exercises, but they must not be treated as official maps, engineering designs or predictions of how a real flood will develop. Why Visual Preparedness Exercises Can Help Conventional awareness materials often use posters, maps and lists of instructions. These remain valuable, especially because they are inexpensive to distribute and easy to print. However, they may not show how several decisions are connected. A tabletop scene can make those relationships easier to discuss. Participants might see a cluster of houses, a school on higher ground, a blocked road, a boat landing point and a temporary shelter. The facilitator can then introduce a scenario: heavy rainfall has continued, an official warning has been issued and one route is no longer usable. The group must decide what information it needs, which official instructions to follow and who may require additional assistance. The model does not provide the answer. It creates a shared setting in which people can explain their reasoning. Make the Scenario Local Without Pretending It Is Exact A training model can reflect familiar features such as stilted homes, village roads, embankments, livestock areas or elevated community buildings. Familiarity makes the exercise easier to understand, but the scene should be clearly labelled as illustrative. Using the name of a real village while inventing roads, water depths or shelter locations could cause confusion. If a session refers to actual geography, the relevant information must come from authorised maps and local disaster-management officials. Build the Exercise Around People, Not Objects A preparedness model becomes more useful when participants consider the needs of different residents. A household with young children faces different constraints from one caring for an older person who has limited mobility. Someone who depends on refrigerated medicine may require a plan for maintaining safe storage. Families with livestock also need instructions appropriate to local arrangements. One possible classroom or community exercise could proceed as follows: • Introduce an imaginary settlement and explain that it is not an official risk map. • Assign participants different household situations. • Present an official warning and close one route in the scenario. • Ask each group what information, supplies and assistance it would need. • Compare the decisions with guidance provided by trained facilitators. • Record questions that should be referred to local authorities. • End by identifying the difference between a classroom scenario and a real emergency. This format encourages participation without asking students or untrained residents to make operational decisions beyond their responsibility. Include Communication Breakdowns Flood exercises should not assume that every participant has continuous internet access, a charged phone or the same level of literacy. The facilitator can introduce a power cut, weak mobile coverage or a message available in only one language. Participants can then discuss how verified information might reach households through several channels. The exercise should reinforce the use of official warnings and recognised local communication networks rather than encouraging people to rely on an unverified social media post. Connect Visual Activities to Official Preparedness Guidance The National Disaster Management Authority's community-based disaster risk reduction guidelines frame communities as active participants in preparedness, response, recovery and risk reduction. A 3D exercise can support this approach when it helps residents identify questions, understand responsibilities and practise communication. It cannot replace official hazard assessments, evacuation planning or emergency drills. Water movement depends on rainfall, river conditions, terrain, drainage and infrastructure. A generated visual scene does not calculate any of these factors. The safest approach is to use the model as a discussion aid within a programme led or reviewed by qualified teachers, disaster-management personnel and local authorities. Review Every Model Before It Enters the Classroom AI-generated assets can contain plausible-looking errors. A boat may have an unrealistic hull, a staircase may be unusable, or a shelter may appear structurally sound despite being only a visual interpretation. Before an exercise, the facilitator should inspect the models for misleading details. Objects should be simplified when realism could imply engineering accuracy. Labels, colours and symbols also need review so that they do not conflict with official materials. Separate Visualisation from Engineering A generated model of a raised house may help explain why people protect documents and supplies above expected water levels. It cannot determine the safe height of a real building or verify its foundation. Likewise, a model of a rescue boat may support a discussion about boarding order and essential supplies, but it cannot establish capacity, stability or operational suitability. Those questions require approved equipment specifications and trained personnel. This distinction should be stated at the beginning and end of every exercise. Design for Schools and Low-Resource Settings A useful preparedness activity should not depend on advanced computers. The models can be shown as still images, short rotations or simple videos if an interactive viewer is impractical. Where 3D printing is available, a few durable objects may be printed for repeated classroom use, but printing is optional. Facilitators should also provide text descriptions and high-contrast diagrams. Students with visual, motor or cognitive disabilities may need tactile elements, additional explanation or alternative ways to participate. Language matters as well. Instructions should use terms understood by the intended community, with translations reviewed by local speakers. A technically correct message can still fail if it is unfamiliar, ambiguous or difficult to read. Measure Learning Through Decisions and Questions The quality of an exercise should not be judged by how realistic its models look. A visually polished scene has limited value if participants leave without knowing where official warnings come from or whom to contact. A better evaluation asks whether participants can distinguish verified information from rumours, identify household members who may need assistance, explain why an evacuation order must be followed and name questions that require an official answer. Teachers can repeat the same scenario later with one condition changed. A route may close earlier, the shelter may become unavailable or communication may fail. Comparing the group's responses can reveal whether participants are applying principles rather than memorising one sequence. Frequently Asked Questions Can AI-generated 3D models predict which areas will flood? No. They are visual assets, not hydrological models. Flood forecasts and risk maps must come from authorised agencies using validated data and appropriate scientific methods. Should students design real evacuation routes with these models? Students may discuss hypothetical choices for learning purposes, but actual evacuation routes and shelter locations must be determined and communicated by responsible authorities. Is 3D printing required for this type of activity? No. Models can be displayed on a screen or converted into still images. The teaching objective should determine the format, particularly where devices, electricity or internet access are limited. Use Technology to Strengthen Preparedness Conversations 3D visualisation can make flood-preparedness training more participatory, particularly when abstract instructions are placed within a recognisable scenario. It can help students ask better questions and help facilitators identify misunderstandings before an emergency. Its role must remain carefully defined. Meshy can accelerate the creation of visual assets for a lesson, while local knowledge, official guidance and trained professionals determine what the exercise should teach. The most effective model is therefore not necessarily the most detailed one. It is the model that encourages people to discuss realistic needs, recognise the limits of their information and understand where to obtain trusted instructions when conditions become dangerous. (The views, opinions, and claims in this article are solely those of the author’s and do not represent the editorial stance of The Assam Tribune)

article_sentences: Three months after a work allocation order led two election commissioners to express concern and raise the matter with Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday issued a fresh order, which, among other changes, brought back the layer of oversight over its Director General (IT), Seema Khanna, that had been removed on July 28.
Under the new order, Senior Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) Pawan Kumar Sharma has been assigned charge of IT/ICT, with Khanna required to route files through him.
“She would put up files of above-mentioned functional divisions through Sr. DEC(PKS),” the order said.
The move effectively reverses a July 28 work allocation order that had removed.
IT and ICT from the charge of then DEC Sanjay Kumar and placed them under Khanna, indicating she would have reported directly to the Commission, instead of a DEC.

The July 28 order led to Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi writing to Somanathan on July 29, saying that Senior DEC Maneesh Garg had issued the same without the Commission’s approval.
While the work allocation order had not been amended till now, the EC has said that it was never implemented following the concerns raised by the two election commissioners.
In effect, Khanna had continued putting up files through Garg, who had been charge of IT as the link officer after Kumar left the EC in August.
“The work allocation order is as per unanimous decision of the Commission.
There is no change in the reporting structure of DG IT.
She has always been reporting to a DEC level officer,” an EC source said Thursday.

After The Indian Express investigation on September 23 revealed that the two election commissioners had written to the Cabinet secretary and petitions were filed in the Supreme Court on the functioning of the Commission, the EC told the court on October 26 that the July 28 work allocation order was issued by an additional secretary-rank officer, Garg.

stories.headline: White House sticks to Trump agenda after midterm election outcome
stories.title: White House sticks to Trump agenda after midterm election outcome
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 5 : The White House has vowed to resist attempts to reverse President Donald Trump's policies during the final two years of his presidency, predicting that Democratic challenges on immigration, taxation, energy and other issues would fail. The White House Office on Wednesday (local time) defended the administration's record and raised the prospect of another impeachment effort, while offering no details of a specific proceeding or legislative proposal. "In the final two years of his presidency, Democrats will try -- and fail -- to reverse everything President Trump has done," the statement said. The release, issued a day after the November 3 midterm elections, portrayed the coming political contest as a defence of Trump's existing policies. It did not announce a new executive action, legislative initiative or negotiating position. "These efforts will fail; the American people have already rejected this agenda," the White House said. The statement placed immigration enforcement prominently among the policies it pledged to defend. It accused Democrats of seeking to undo border restrictions and large-scale deportations, presenting those predictions as part of a broader attack on the opposition. It did not identify specific Democratic bills or statements supporting each of the intentions it attributed to the party. Its descriptions of what Democrats would pursue were the administration's political assertions, rather than an agreed account of the opposition's programme. On the economy, the White House defended Trump's tax cuts and claimed they had delivered record growth. It also credited the administration with record energy production and what it described as American energy independence. The release did not provide figures, time periods or comparisons to substantiate those economic and energy claims. It linked to a separate White House account of Trump's second-term record. Law enforcement was another focus. The statement claimed that Trump had produced the largest decline in violent crime in modern history, but did not include supporting crime statistics or specify the period covered by that comparison. The White House also pledged to defend its actions against diversity, equity and inclusion programmes, commonly known as DEI. It accused Democrats of seeking to restore those programmes and reverse administration policies affecting transgender minors. Other passages alleged that Democrats would rebuild censorship mechanisms and weaken efforts to curb waste, fraud and abuse. The statement did not identify particular measures underpinning those accusations. The White House accused Democrats of wanting to expand the Supreme Court and predicted another attempt to impeach Trump. It did not name lawmakers pursuing those steps or describe a formal proposal. The release characterised the President's earlier impeachment proceedings as failed efforts and said future attempts to reverse his agenda would meet the same outcome. The message was a pledge of continued political resistance: "President Trump will never stop fighting." --IANS

stories.headline: Failure To Seek Recount During Counting Alone Does Not Justify Rejecting An Election Petition: Chhattisgarh High Court
stories.title: Failure To Seek Recount During Counting Alone Does Not Justify Rejecting An Election Petition: Chhattisgarh High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Chhattisgarh High Court has upheld an Election Tribunal's decision refusing to reject an election petition merely because the election petitioner had not sought recounting of votes during the counting process.
The Court held that specific allegations of discrepancies in vote tabulation and manipulation of election records raised triable issues which required adjudication on evidence.

Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad was hearing a writ petition filed by the returned candidate challenging the Election Tribunal's rejection of his application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking rejection of an election petition.
The election petition had raised a challenge to the election of the petitioner, alleging irregularities in the counting and tabulation of votes at Polling Booth No. 187.

The returned candidate argued that recounting was not sought during the counting process on February 23, 2025, as contemplated under Rule 80(1) read with Rule 80(5) of the Chhattisgarh Panchayat Nirvachan Niyam, 1995.
Relying on Supreme Court decisions, he contended that the election petition was not maintainable in the absence of a request for recounting at the appropriate stage.
The Court noted that while deciding an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC, the court must examine the election petition as a whole and determine whether its pleadings disclose a cause of action.
The defence raised by the returned candidate and disputed questions requiring evidence cannot ordinarily be considered at this preliminary stage.
The Court observed that the absence of a recounting request during counting did not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of examining the entire election petition.

“The mere fact that no request for recounting was made at the time of counting does not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of examining the entire election petition to determine whether it discloses a cause of action or is ex facie barred by law,” the Court remarked.
The Court further noted that the election petitioner had explained that the discrepancies became apparent only after he obtained the certified tabulation chart.
The Court clarified that it was not deciding whether this explanation was ultimately sufficient or whether the allegations were true; those questions were for the Election Tribunal to determine.

stories.headline: Salman faces backlash over 'Teri Sexy Beauty' song in Maatrubhumi
stories.title: Salman faces backlash over 'Teri Sexy Beauty' song in Maatrubhumi
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 5 : Bollywood superstar Salman Khan has found himself at the receiving end of severe criticism on social media after unveiling his latest song, ‘Teri Sexy Beauty’, from his upcoming film Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace. While the actor's return to playback singing after 11 years has grabbed attention, the song has left a section of netizens baffled. Many questioned its relevance in a film based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops. The song, featuring Salman Khan and Chitrangda Singh, was released in the early hours of November 4. Salman also shared a video announcing the track on social media with a rather cheeky caption. "Departure time 5:12 am…. Flight on time , 2 pegs down taking off with my sexy beauty… pata nahi kahaan mai land karoon #TeriSexyBeauty Out Now" The song features Salman crooning alongside Muskaan, with additional vocals by Sajid Khan. It shows Chitrangada Singh in a red saree with Salman also dancing, and the both sharing some romantic and flirtation moments along with a couple of drinks. The song's lyrics and picturisation have not gone down well with a section of the audience, particularly considering the sensitivity of the film's subject. Soon after its release, several X users questioned how a song with lyrics such as "Teri sexy beauty ka fan ban gaya hoon, main do peg pee ke aeroplane ban gaya hoon" could feature in a patriotic film inspired by the sacrifice of Indian Army personnel. One user wrote, "A film based on Col. Santosh Babu & 19 soldiers beaten to death in Galwan and Salman’s tribute is ‘Teri sexy beauty ka fan ho gaya hu, 2 peg peeke talli ho gaya hu.’ How can anyone even think of putting a song like this in a patriotic film. He has zero respect for real martyrs." Another user commented, "Real story pe based patriotic movie me ye sab kya lyrics hai gende. Ek national hero ke character ko kiya bana diya." Another netizen expressed disappointment over the film's changing narrative and musical choices, writing in Hindi that a patriotic film's title, script and songs had seemingly undergone changes. It added that a romantic number now has taken the place of what audiences expected from a film about soldiers. The criticism did not stop there. Many users also took a dig at Salman Khan's singing, with one calling the lyrics "ChatGPT lyrics", while another wrote, "Salmon bhai ruining his own legacy....." A particularly critical user urged the superstar to retire, writing, "Salman Khan, if you don’t want to work properly like you did before 2016, just retire. Please, don’t destroy what’s left of your reputation! Don’t you see, notice, or listen to what you’re actually doing?" Another user sarcastically told the actor, "Bhai. Aap ab bas udd hi jaao," referring to the aeroplane references in the song. However, not everyone was disappointed. Some fans came out in support of Salman, appreciating the catchy tune and his return to singing. For the unversed, Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace which was earlier titled Battle of Galwan, is inspired by the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian Army personnel, including Colonel Bikkumalla Santosh Babu, lost their lives. Salman essays the role of an Army officer, while Chitrangda Singh plays his wife. –IANS

Lower fuel prices improve the operating economics of truck and bus owners, potentially encouraging fleet expansion, replacement demand and fresh vehicle purchases. Cheaper crude also reduces input and logistics costs for automakers, supporting margins. Additionally, lower fuel prices can ease inflationary pressures and improve overall economic activity, benefiting freight movement and transportation demand.2.) stories.title: Supreme Court Expresses Reservations Over Judgment Holding Right To Speedy Trial Cannot Override Stringent NDPS Bail Conditions

article_sentences: The Court observed that the right to speedy trial, being a fundamental right, cannot be subjected to stringent bail conditions.

The Supreme Court's two-judge bench today expressed reservations about another two-judge bench's judgment in Sukhwinder Singh (2026), which held that the right to speedy trial under Article 21 can't override the stringent statutory requirements for granting bail under Section 37 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1987 (NDPS).

In the verdict pronounced today in Sujit Das v UOI, a bench comprising Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S Chandurkar expressed that the judgment in State of Punjab v Sukhwinder Singh @ Gora has become "per incuriam" in the light of the 2021 UOI v KA Najeeb judgment, wherein a three-judge bench held that violation of the right to speedy trial is a ground for constitutional Courts to grant bail even under special statutes which provide for stringent bail conditions.
The bench said: "In Sukhwinder Singh alias Gora, this Court observed that the right to speedy trial rooted in Article 21 of the Constitution is undoubtedly a precious constitutional right.

However, the bench proceeded to observe that in matters governed by special enactments such as the NDPS Act, particularly where the recovery is of commercial quantity, the said right under Article 21 must be exercised within the framework of Section 37 and cannot be pressed into service only on the ground of delay to override Section 37."

Noting this, Justice Bhuyan, who read the pronouncement, stated that while the coordinate bench comprising Justice Sanjay Karol and Justice AG Masih stated that Article 21 and Section 37 of the NDPS Act are to be read harmoniously and not placed in opposition to each other, the present bench feels that when the former is violated, the rigours of special enactments will melt down as held in Najeeb.
He said: "We have our reservations on the aforesaid observations made by the bench.
First and foremost, the rights conferred by Article 21 of the Constitution are not only constitutional rights, these are fundamental rights.
The right to life and liberty as enshrined in Article 21 are at the core of our constitutional jurisprudence.
These fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under a special statute."

Further, the bench stated that the observations in Sukhwinder run counter to numerous judgments where it has been reiterated that when there is a violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the rigour of Section 37 of the NDPS Act or similar provisions under a special statute would have to give way.

Referring to those judgments, the bench said: "Please see Union of India versus K A Najeeb, Satender Kumar Antil, Mohd Muslim, Ankur Chadda, Vijay Singh versus Union of India, where this Court clearly held that Article 21 of the Constitution of India overrides Section 37 of the NDPS Act.

article_sentences: 96% of Person to Merchant transactions would remain free, the NPCI stated.

Defending its decision to levy charges for transactions above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payment Interface (UPI), the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has told the Supreme Court that merchants are barred from passing on MDR charges to customers.
It has further stated that UPI application providers cannot impose platform fees or other charges for UPI payments.

“Second, non-compliance by a Payer PSP or TPAP with the NPCI Circular's directive against passing on MDR to customers constitutes a breach of the binding obligation under the SLAs to abide by all circulars, orders, directions and instructions issued by the Answering Respondent, and exposes such Payer PSP or TPAP to compliance actions which may also lead to termination of its UPI membership and facilities.

Therefore, the non-pass-through directive to the banks and UPI service providers is a mandatory and binding direction, which is enforceable through contractual mechanism in place, and is not a mere 'assurance' or a matter of policy.
Thus, apprehension that the consumers are left exposed to an indirect burden is accordingly without any foundation”, the affidavit states.

NPCI has filed a counter affidavit filed on November 3 in a petition challenging the amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, introduced through the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, the subsequent Ministry of Finance notification and the revised MDR framework announced in September.

The Supreme Court had in September 2026 sought an affidavit explaining the basis for the move to levy charges for transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI) above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants.

NPCI has submitted that around 96% of person-to-merchant transactions will remain unaffected by the revised MDR, the NPCI has refuted the apprehension that the MDR charges would cause merchants to increase prices.

“The charge under the MDR is attracted only to a small fraction i.e. approximately 4%, of P2M transactions that exceed INR 2,000 and thus, a measure confined so narrowly in its incidence affords less scope for merchants to recalibrate their pricing across their entire customer base merely on account of a charge that arises only occasionally and only above a defined value.
Accordingly, the apprehension that the MDR Framework will result in quiet revision of prices is also misconceived”, the NPCI has stated.
NPCI has stated that person-to-person transactions and transactions involving small merchants under the P2PM category will continue to remain free.

stories.headline: Supreme Court says 24-hour arrest deadline begins when person is detained
stories.title: Supreme Court says 24-hour arrest deadline begins when person is detained
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour deadline for producing an arrested person before a magistrate begins from the moment their liberty is curtailed, and not from the time the police formally record the arrest.
A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that excluding the period of detention before a formal arrest from the 24-hour deadline would violate Article 22(2) of the Constitution.
The ruling came in appeals filed by four people challenging the Tripura High Court's rejection of their bail pleas in a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.
The four accused were detained on September 29, 2025, at around 2 pm during a search and seizure operation.
However, the police formally recorded their arrest only at 11 am the following day.
The Supreme Court held that they should have been produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of their detention on September 29.
According to a LiveLaw report, the court found that the accused had been kept in custody for around 18 hours without judicial oversight, violating their constitutional rights.
It consequently ordered their immediate release.
"Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for inquiry or investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee," the bench observed.
The court clarified that the only period that can be excluded while calculating the 24-hour deadline is the time required to travel from the place of arrest to the magistrate's court.
It rejected the argument that detention before a formal arrest should be treated differently, observing that fundamental rights cannot be temporarily suspended during an investigation.

The bench also disapproved of earlier rulings by the Orissa High Court in Aryaman Pattanaik, the Kerala High Court in Arun K Thomas and the Madras High Court in Kannan, which had allowed pre-arrest detention to be excluded from the 24-hour calculation.

article_sentences: The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that it is planning to put in place a committee to reconsider the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, which were stayed by the court earlier this year after petitions questioned their neutrality.
“The government is contemplating appointing a committee,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a three-judge bench presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
The solicitor general said this after the bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana told the government to consider taking a relook at the provisions.
“Why don’t you revisit these regulations so that the next generation is taken care of?
They should protect the interest of every student,” the CJI said.

Notified on January 13 this year, the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, snowballed into a political issue after drawing objections from both general category groups and sections of Dalit and OBC communities.

In the eye of the storm is regulation 3(1)(c), which defines caste-based discrimination as discrimination on the basis of caste or tribe against members of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes.
Petitioners who challenged it argued that this excludes general category students and faculty from specific protection against caste-based discrimination.
At the same time, the regulations’ broader definition of “discrimination” covers unfair or differential treatment on the ground of caste against any stakeholder.

The regulations stem from a 2019 petition filed in the Supreme Court by the mothers of Payal Tadvi and Rohith Vemula, who died by suicide over alleged caste-based discrimination in 2019 and 2016, respectively.
They had sought the enforcement of robust anti-discrimination mechanisms across higher education institutions.

stories.headline: Supreme Court panel seeks comprehensive re-examination of UP govt’s Kukrail night safari project plans
stories.title: Supreme Court panel seeks comprehensive re-examination of UP govt’s Kukrail night safari project plans
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC), an environmental watchdog for monitoring compliance with the court’s directions on forests, has said the Uttar Pradesh government should undertake a comprehensive ‘re-examination’ of its entire Kukrail night safari and zoological park project in Lucknow.
The exercise should involve revisiting the plans, environmental clearances and other approvals for the project for conformity with the court’s July 15 order, and the CEC’s own recommendations.

In a status report submitted to the SC dated October 27, the CEC said that following a site inspection and review meeting held on September 10 it found “visible disturbance” to the undergrowth and forest floor, including soil-levelling, and discrepancies in trees inventoried for felling.
These activities were observed, the CEC said, even though the site had not been formally handed to the Public Works Department by the Forest Department.
While the panel has not concluded that any violation occurred, it said the authority under which the work was done, its extent and its permissibility “require verification from the relevant records”.
The CEC’s ‘status report’ was submitted in compliance with the Supreme Court’s July 15 order, which had allowed the Kukrail night safari and zoological park project subject to strict conditions.
The Kukrail project, estimated to cost Rs 1,510.57 crore, is proposed in the Kukrail forest in the northeastern part of Lucknow.
The court had directed the CEC to conduct periodic inspections and verify compliance with conditions and safeguards contained in a 2025 CEC report, and the Central Zoo Authority.

Even though the SC permitted the Uttar Pradesh government to proceed with the project in July 2026, it agreed with the CEC’s recommendations to reject key proposed components—the moving of the Nawab Wajid Ali Shah Zoological Park, building an adventure park, and widening of a road into four lanes.

The CEC said that the revised DPR and Master Plan should be finalised only after a substantive re-examination of the project layout and footprint, reconciliation of the tree inventory with ground conditions, verification of land boundaries, and mapping of nature drainage channels, seasonal streams, wetlands and microhabitats.

“All proposed components should be examined for conformity with the order dated 15.07.2026 of this Hon’ble Court…activity requiring a statutory approval or permissions should not commence until that approval or permission has been obtained,” the CEC said in the status report.

On the issue of approvals, the CEC stated that the UP government shall examine whether any amendment, modification, revision or additional approval is required in the detailed project report, master plan, environmental clearance or other project documents to ensure conformity with applicable orders and conditions.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi calls BJP’s Gokul move ‘theft of votes’
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP of seeking to overturn the Gokul milk union election result through government-appointed directors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday accused the BJP of attempting to wrest control of Maharashtra’s Gokul milk union by changing the cooperative law after the Congress-led panel secured a narrow majority in its board election.

The criticism followed the Maharashtra cabinet’s approval on Wednesday of an amendment allowing the government to appoint five directors, four with voting rights, to certain large cooperative societies receiving state assistance.
At the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul, the Congress-led panel headed by Satej Patil won 13 of the 25 elected seats on 19 October.
The BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12.
The proposed appointments could change that balance ahead of the chairman’s election scheduled for 10 November under a Bombay High Court direction.
If all four voting nominees support the Mahayuti-backed directors, their combined strength would rise to 16 against the Congress-led panel’s 13.
Rahul Gandhi described the proposal as an attempt to reverse the verdict delivered by milk producers.
“This is theft of the milk producers’ votes — adulteration in the mandate,” he wrote on X.
He accused the BJP of changing the rules after losing the election and warned that farmers would remember the move.
The cabinet, chaired by chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, approved a proposal to amend Section 73AA(2) of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, through an ordinance.
The provision would apply to cooperative societies with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore that receive government assistance in the form of funds, land, loans or guarantees.
District Central Cooperative Banks would be exempt.
